questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good reputation of Heidelberg University Hospital and the opportunity to improve my German language skills and broaden my career opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information from the University of Copenhagen and Heidelberg University was easy to find and well coordinated but there was very little information regarding clinical rotations and the first days in the clinic were a bit chaotic.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received little assistance, mostly information from medical students who has previously completed their rotation in Heidelberg.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The communication for medical students doing clinical rotations could be improved so that the receiving departments were informed of our arrival and stay.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy as I was put in contact with a landlord by a former exhange student.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great way to meet "locals" and practice your language skills.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was put in contact with a coordinator who arranged my clinical rotations according to my study plan and priorities.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both Erasmus coordinators at the University of Copenhagen and Heidelberg University were available to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to complete rotations in the departments I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the coordinators early and reconfirm your stay and rotations before your arrival.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I was doing clinical rotations at the hospital, mainly in the emergency departments. This meant a high patient flow and opportunity to see and treat many different conditions.
I did my internal medicine rotation in the internal medicine ER (internistische Notfallambulanz), my surgery rotations in the surgical ER (Chirurgischen Ambulanz) and anaesthesia in Kopfklinik.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Supervision and teaching varied a lot between departments and mostly depended on the doctors as there was no structured programmed for us.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anaesthesia (ECTS 2,5)
Internal medicine (ECTS 7,5)
Surgery (ECTS 7,5)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I can highly recommend anaesthesia in Kopfklinik. The doctors are very nice and helpful, they are great at teaching and supervising and you get lots of hands-on training in many practical skills. 

Internal medicine in internistische Notfallambulanz also gives you the opportunity to see many patients with a broad spectrum of internal presentations as well as practice many clinical skills. 

Chirurgischen Ambulanz tends to have many students and less patients which means you do not get to see many patients compared to the other places.

questions.answer: Organic fruit and vegetables were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offers many sports activities for a very cheap price compared to other places in Heidelberg.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a local sportsclub to meet people outside campus and get a chance to practice your German.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are many great one-day or weekend trips from Heidelberg including München, Nürnberg, Freiburg, Paris and Luxembourg.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I found everyone to be helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join sports activities at campus or visit bars in the city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any challenging cultural differences but you have to adjust to a different hierarchy among students and doctors in the clinic compared to Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Heidelberg is a great city with a relaxed atmosphere and beautiful nature nearby.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make an effort to learn the language.
2. Enjoy the city and make use of the beautiful surroundings.  
3. Join a local club to meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make an effort to speak the language and be active in the clinic. Often you can find a couple of doctors in your department who have time and interest in teaching clinical skills and helping you practice. Be aware of what skills you wish or need to practice and make an effort to pursue them. Sometimes you can learn a lot from showing up in the evening or weekend shifts where there are less students and therefore more work.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my German language skills and getting an insight into another health care system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting the most out of all clinical rotations and align the purpose of my rotation and level of clinical skill as this was different from the German medical students who are either doing rotations early in their studies or as part of their final year.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
